outcome: Risk of obstetric anal sphincter injuries (OASIS)
cohort: 1340 term nulliparous women with singleton pregnancies who underwent an instrumental delivery or fully dilated caesarean section
finding: Doctors preferring forceps for instrumental delivery reported a lower rate of obstetric anal sphincter injuries and a higher rate of fully dilated caesarean sections compared to those preferring vacuum.
mod_finding: The overall risk of OASIS is higher for forceps compared to vacuum deliveries. Doctors with a preference for forceps compared to vacuum, correlated with both a lower OASIS rate and a higher fully dilated caesarean section rate.
